events.title: .NET Core 1.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft released .NET Core 1.0 on June 27, 2016 — a cross-platform, open-source fork of .NET for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
events.about: .NET Core broke .NET free from Windows-only deployment: ASP.NET APIs on Linux containers, microservices on macOS dev machines, and MIT-licensed runtime code. It evolved into modern .NET 5+ and replaced .NET Framework for new cloud and cross-platform projects.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET Core was Microsoft's pivot to open, cross-platform server development.
narrative.whyImportant: Linux and Docker support made C# viable outside the Windows data center.
narrative.problemSolved: .NET Framework was Windows-only; cloud-native teams needed the CLR on Linux.
